---
title: "TD, PD and FD on one scale"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev.args = list(bg = "white"), collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dpi = 150)
```

tidydiversity measures three dimensions of diversity with the same Hill
number framework:

* **Taxonomic diversity (TD)** treats every species as equally distinct.
* **Phylogenetic diversity (PD)** weights species by the branch lengths of
  a phylogeny (Chao, Chiu and Jost 2010, 2014).
* **Functional diversity (FD)** weights species by their trait distances,
  using the attribute-diversity approach of Chao et al. (2019).

Each is an effective number of species of order `q`, so the three can be
plotted on the same axis. The estimators reproduce
[iNEXT.3D](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=iNEXT.3D) and this is checked
in the package test suite.

## Data

The example uses the Brazilian rainforest tree data shipped with iNEXT.3D:
abundances at two sites (`Edge` and `Interior`), a time-calibrated
phylogeny and a Gower distance matrix of traits.

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

data(list = c(
  "Brazil_rainforest_abun_data", "Brazil_rainforest_phylo_tree",
  "Brazil_rainforest_distance_matrix"
), package = "iNEXT.3D")
wide <- Brazil_rainforest_abun_data
brazil <- tibble(
  site = rep(colnames(wide), each = nrow(wide)),
  species = rep(rownames(wide), ncol(wide)),
  n = unlist(wide, use.names = FALSE)
) |>
  filter(n > 0)
tree <- Brazil_rainforest_phylo_tree
traits <- as.matrix(Brazil_rainforest_distance_matrix)
```

## Observed and asymptotic diversity {.tabset}

### TD

```{r}
div_estimate(brazil, abundance = n, nboot = 0)
```

### PD

`reftime` defaults to the age of the root of the tree pruned to the observed
species. With `pd_unit = "mean"` (the default) PD is divided by `reftime`,
giving the effective number of lineages.

```{r}
div_estimate(brazil, abundance = n, type = "PD", tree = tree)
```

### FD

`tau` defaults to the mean distance between two individuals in the pooled
data. Species closer than `tau` count as functionally identical.

```{r}
div_estimate(brazil, abundance = n, type = "FD", distance = traits)
```

### FD (area under the tau profile)

`tau = "auc"` integrates FD over every threshold from 0 to 1, so no single
threshold has to be chosen.

```{r}
div_estimate(brazil, abundance = n, type = "FD", distance = traits, tau = "auc")
```

## Standardised comparison

Standardise every dimension to the same sample coverage. Coverage is
computed from the species counts, as in iNEXT.3D, and the PD and FD values
are then evaluated at the matching sample size.

```{r}
dims <- list(
  TD = list(),
  PD = list(type = "PD", tree = tree),
  FD = list(type = "FD", distance = traits)
)
std <- bind_rows(lapply(names(dims), function(d) {
  args <- c(list(brazil, abundance = quote(n), coverage = 0.97, nboot = 0), dims[[d]])
  do.call(div_standardise, args) |> mutate(type = d)
}))
std |> select(type, site, q, m, coverage, diversity)
```

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Diversity profiles at 97 percent coverage for TD, PD and FD at two sites."}
ggplot(std, aes(q, diversity, colour = site)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~type, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(y = "Effective number of species", colour = NULL) +
  theme_tidydiversity()
```

## Current limits

* Bootstrap standard errors and confidence intervals are available for TD
  only. For PD and FD, `se`, `lower` and `upper` are `NA`.
* Incidence data are not yet supported for PD and FD.

## References

Chao, A., Chiu, C.-H. and Jost, L. (2014). Unifying species diversity,
phylogenetic diversity, functional diversity, and related similarity and
differentiation measures through Hill numbers. *Annual Review of Ecology,
Evolution, and Systematics*, 45, 297-324.
<https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-ecolsys-120213-091540>

Chao, A., Chiu, C.-H., Villeger, S. et al. (2019). An attribute-diversity
approach to functional diversity, functional beta diversity, and related
(dis)similarity measures. *Ecological Monographs*, 89, e01343.
<https://doi.org/10.1002/ecm.1343>
